Maya G: Quick heads-up — we're seeing a mismatch between the Console's "estimated units" and runtime billing/quotas for mixed-dim embedding requests. acme-inc hit repeated throttles that don't line up with what Console showed.
Sam R: Can you paste an example request/estimate?
Maya G: Yep — minimal repro. Console shows ~4 units, runtime consumed ~9 and then we throttled.
Maya G: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","inputs":[{"text":"short","dim":512},{"text":"long","dim":1536}]}'
```
Sam R: Interesting. Do we still infer dims server side? I thought Console estimated using declared shape if present.
Luca: We do dim detection server-side and our runtime charges against the max-dim in the batch for unit accounting. Console estimate currently uses a simple heuristic that averages per-item dims to show an "expected" units number — which explains underestimates for mixed batches.
Jen (console): Oof. That heuristic was for UX simplicity but it's misleading. We should either mirror runtime logic or show a confidence/warning. Rolling a silent fix might break customers who rely on Console numbers.
Sam R: Two immediate mitigations: 1) surface a warning in the Console whenever inputs are mixed-dim, 2) add a telemetry counter for estimate!=runtime to quantify impact.
Maya G: Agreed. Also consider asking clients to opt-in to an explicit header `X-Embed-Shape: <dims>` to let Console and router agree. If header absent, runtime keeps current behavior.
Luca: Header approach is nice but it's a client opt-in and won't fix existing traffic. We could change Console to compute estimate = max(dim) per request (mirror runtime) and mark it as "charged units (runtime)", then slowly roll out.
Jen (console): Implementation plan: show a yellow banner for mixed-dim requests today, change the estimator logic behind a feature flag to use `max(dim)` for the UI, ship flag, monitor `embed.unit_mismatch` metric, then flip flag after 1 week of sanity.
Sam R: I'll add the feature-flagged estimator and the banner. ETA: end of day tomorrow for a canary.
Luca: I'll add telemetry: `embed.unit_mismatch{tenant, route, sample}` and a histogram for runtime_units vs console_estimate. Also add an alert if mismatch_rate > 5% over 1h for a tenant.
Maya G: I'll reach out to ACME CS and schedule a debrief. Also add them to the canary list so they see the corrected estimates first.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: console/estimator-feature-flag -> canary -> 2026-03-23T02:00Z
Sam R: Quick note on UX copy — make the banner say: "Mixed embedding shapes detected. Console estimate may undercount actual charged units. Consider adding `X-Embed-Shape` from your client to improve estimates."
Jen (console): Copy sounds good. Also add a link to our public doc snippet showing recommended header usage and examples.
Luca: One more engineering question: for the estimator feature flag, should the console call the preflight API to get a canonical units estimate from the router, or copy the router logic locally? Preflight call adds latency and extra load.
Sam R: I'd prefer local logic parity first (fast), then a background preflight sample job to validate and surface discrepancies. If we see drift, we can switch the flag to call preflight for the canary group.
Maya G: Action items summary: Sam -> flag + banner + canary; Luca -> telemetry + alert + histogram; Jen -> UX copy + doc link + canary list; Maya -> CS outreach + canary onboarding.
Sam R: I'll create the PR and tag you all. @Luca @Jen please review the telemetry schema when I post it.
Jen (console): 👍 thanks.
Maya G: Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread open for updates.
